# Sensor Pipeline: plan and status The official plan for Green Thumb's sensor-side pipeline, from the I2C seam up to the 16 B message a sensor process sends to the hub and the 24 B record the hub sends to storage. That covers the BH1750 light-sensor driver and the shared pieces it relies on: sensor health tracking, the log line formatter, the sensor→hub message and the hub→storage record codec, plus the IPC client that carries the 16 B message over `hub.sock`. A new session should be able to read this file, plus `CLAUDE.md` and `DESIGN.md`, and pick up where work stopped without re-explanation. Since 2026-10-26 the file also holds a second top-level part, *Mechanism D: storage*, with its own Goal, Code map, Decisions, Status, *Not done yet* and Log. So there are two Status sections: **Status** (the sensor pipeline and IPC, Steps 0–24) and **Status (Mechanism D)** (storage). **Update either Status section only at the end of the day, when asked.** ## Context - **Owner:** Lily (DESIGN.md → Ownership map: "Light sensor (driver and process)" and "IPC (data path)"). - **Goal of this phase:** prove the sensor is *electrically alive* and *trustworthy* before it is connected to the data pipeline. That means the bus opens, the chip ACKs, reads decode, failures are retried and bounded, and a sensor that keeps failing is marked offline instead of silently producing nothing. Then pin the wire message the light process will send. - **Goal of the IPC phase (Steps 10–24):** a reading leaves the sensor process and reaches a hub stand-in (`hub_listen`) over `hub.sock`. It survives the hub being killed and restarted (buffered, then resent in order, or covered by a GAP), and the client never blocks the 1 Hz sampling. - **Hardware:** BH1750 on `/dev/i2c-1` at address `0x23` (ADDR pin low or floating). Continuous high-res mode at 1 lx/count; each conversion takes at most 180 ms. Lux = raw / 1.2. **Raw counts are stored, never lux.** - **Sampling rate:** 1 Hz (DESIGN.md). The 1 Hz schedule belongs to the sampler, not the driver. - **Rule from DESIGN.md's failure-mode table (Sensor (I2C) row):** retry 3× at 10 ms, then skip the sample. After 10 consecutive failures, mark the sensor offline and retry every 5 s. Log `i2c_read_error`, `sensor_offline` and `sensor_online`. ## Design principle - **Layered seam:** `src/i2c_bus.c` is the only file that makes I2C system calls. The driver talks to the bus only through `gt_i2c_ops` (`write` / `read` / `sleep_ms` / `close`). A clean first connect fires no event. - **Backoff:** the waits run 100 → 200 → 400 → 800 → 1600 → 2000 ms, then stay at 2000 ms, so attempts fall at 0, 100, 300, 700, 1500, 3100, 5100 ms… Any successful connect resets the wait to 100 ms. - **Ring:** 64 slots × 16 B (≈1 KB, DESIGN.md resource budget). Each message is encoded when it enters the ring, so a bad message is rejected (`GT_ERR_INVAL`) before it takes a slot. Frames leave only when `send` returns OK. - **What `send` returns to the caller:** - `GT_OK`: the message was sent or buffered. - `GT_ERR_FULL`: it was refused and counted. - `GT_ERR_INVAL`: bad arguments or a bad message. A disconnect is not an error to the caller: it is reported through the event flags. - **Overflow:** - **Ring full:** the new reading is refused, `refused` goes up by one, and the client remembers the first refused counter. `EV_OVERFLOW` fires once per overflow run, not once per refusal. - **Gap pending:** the next reading is accepted only when **2 slots** are free. The client then enqueues the GAP `{type = GAP, sensor_id, counter = first refused, value = refused count}`, followed by the reading. With fewer than 2 free slots, the reading is refused into the same gap. - **Order on the wire:** the buffered old data, then the GAP, then the new data. - **`pump`:** does the same connect-and-drain as `send` without a new message. The sensor loop calls it every tick, so the ring still drains while the sensor is offline and not producing readings. - **Close:** sends nothing and calls `destroy` once. 272	- **Rollover failure logs every second:** while a new segment can't be created, `segment_create_error` is logged on every 1 s tick.
273	- **The 1970 file:** a Pi that boots with no network time and an empty log writes `log-19700101.bin` until NTP syncs (acknowledged in Lucas's *Not done yet*).
274	- **Resolution (2026-10-27):**
275	  - **Unique `.corrupt` names:** a second `.corrupt` copy of the same segment no longer replaces the first. Recovery picks the first free name of `<name>.corrupt`, `<name>.2.corrupt` … `<name>.99.corrupt` (SRV-12). Every name still ends in `.corrupt`, so `log_verify` counts them.
276	  - **Retention and the 128-name limit:** `.corrupt` files are still never deleted (decided 2026-10-27: they are evidence). The limit is now documented in `storage.h` and DESIGN.md: more than 128 names stops storage at start with `storage_open_error`, and the fix is to clear old `.corrupt` files by hand.
277	  - **`segment_create_error`:** it is now logged once per failure spell, and the next successful rollover re-arms it (FTK-12).
278	  - **The 1970 file (decided 2026-10-27):** on an empty log with an unsynced clock, `storage_main` now waits up to 120 s for the clock before open names the first segment. It logs `clock_wait max_s=120`, then `clock_wait_done waited_s=N synced=0|1`. The hub's 1024-record queue covers the wait. 279	  - **Still possible:** with no network for the whole 120 s, it still starts a 1970 file. That stays a documented limit in `storage.h` and DESIGN.md.
280	  - **Not tested yet:** the wait itself has not been seen running, because WSL's clock is always synced. It needs a check on the Pi with the network unplugged.
281	  - **Doc follow-up (2026-10-27):** Sensor-Pipeline.md's *Not done yet (Mechanism D)* still listed "the 1970 file" as unfixed, saying a proper fix meant `storage_main` waiting for the clock. That wait now exists, so the bullet was reworded to the open item: the on-Pi check of the clock wait.

285	**DESIGN.md**
286	- **`storage_main.c` start-up order:** the one-listener lock, then recovery, then bind `storage.sock`, then the flush thread, then the rx loop. A second copy refuses to start.
287	- **Shutdown:** on SIGTERM, storage takes any records already in the socket, joins the flush thread, does the final flush, and writes the clean-shutdown marker only if that flush succeeded. 288	- **Recovery:** marker check, newest-segment header check and `.corrupt` rename, scan to the first bad record (magic, type, version, CRC, `seq`, partial tail), truncate + fsync, then the walk back for the last `seq`.
289	- **Durability:** fsync per batch; directory fsync when a segment is created; on a failed write or fsync the batch stays pending, storage is marked degraded, and the next cycle truncates to the last committed offset before rewriting.

292	- **Locking:** the mutex is never held during file I/O.

No other process writes to the log. See the *Architecture Diagram* (storage subgraph) and *Mechanism mapping → Mechanism D*. 182 183 ### What is stored 184 185 The log holds two kinds of fixed-size record: 186 187 - **DATA record:** one accepted reading from one sensor. It holds the sensor ID, the hub-assigned sequence number, a timestamp and the sensor's **raw count**: 188 - Light (BH1750): raw 16-bit count. Lux = count / 1.2, converted when the data is read. 189 - Soil (STEMMA seesaw): raw capacitance count, roughly 200–2000. 190 191 Light and soil are stored as separate records, not combined into one row. Raw counts are stored rather than converted units, so calibration can change later without rewriting history. 192 - **GAP record:** an explicit marker that readings were refused. It holds the affected sensor, the gap's start time and the number of refused readings. The component that refuses the readings writes the gap record (sensor ring, hub queue or storage queue). See the rule above the *Failure-mode table*. 193 194 Readings that fail validation (out of range, or a malformed message) are rejected by the hub and are **not** stored. See the *Failure-mode table → Hub* rows. 195 196 The timestamp is applied by the hub when it receives the reading. If the Pi booted without network time, the timestamps may be wrong until NTP syncs. Ordering always comes from `seq`. See the *Failure-mode table → System clock*. 197 198 ### At what rate 199 200 | Stream | Rate | Records/day | 201 |---|---|---| 202 | Light | 1 per second | 86,400 | 203 | Soil | 1 per 60 s | 1,440 | 204 | **Total into storage** | **≈1.02 records/s (≈25 B/s)** | **87,840 ≈ 2.1 MB/day** | 205 206 On the wire, each reading travels sensor → hub as a 16 B socket message (layout under *In what format*). Hub → storage carries the 24 B record itself, laid out exactly as on disk with the CRC included: the hub stamps the timestamp when the reading arrives and `seq` + CRC when it sends the record, and storage checks the magic, version, type, sensor and CRC before appending it. On disk, each reading is one 24 B record. Gap records only appear during failures and add negligible volume. See the *Architecture Diagram* data path labels. 207 208 ### In what format 209 210 The log is an **append-only binary log** of fixed 24 B records, packed and little-endian. 211 212 **Segment header** (16 B, written once at the start of each file): 213 214 | Field | Size | Value | 215 |---|---|---| 216 | magic | 4 B | `"GTLG"` | 217 | version | 2 B | 1 | 218 | record_size | 2 B | 24 | 219 | created_at | 8 B | µs since the Unix epoch | 220 221 **Record** (24 B): 222 223 | Field | Size | DATA record | GAP record | 224 |---|---|---|---| 225 | magic | 1 B | `0xA7` | `0xA7` | 226 | record_type | 1 B | `0x01` | `0x02` | 227 | version | 1 B | 1 | 1 | 228 | sensor_id | 1 B | 1 = light, 2 = soil | affected sensor (0 = all) | 229 | seq | 4 B | hub sequence number | see below | 230 | timestamp | 8 B | hub receive time, µs since epoch | gap start, µs since epoch | 231 | value | 4 B | raw sensor count (u32) | refused-reading count (u32) | 232 | crc32 | 4 B | CRC-32 over bytes 0–19 | CRC-32 over bytes 0–19 | 233 234 - A gap ends at the timestamp of the next DATA record for the same sensor, so it needs no separate end field. 235 - Every record has a `seq`, and `seq` is strictly increasing across the log: 236 - Gaps created by a sensor or by the hub receive a hub-assigned `seq`. 237 - Gaps created by storage use the `seq` of the first refused reading. Their timestamp is that of the last record storage accepted before the gap: the earliest moment the gap could have started, since the missing readings' own times are lost with them. After a restart, recovery supplies it from the newest record on disk. A storage gap (`sensor_id` 0) ends at the next record of any sensor. 238 - Any record with an unknown `record_type` is treated as corrupt. 239 240 **Storage → hub `seq_resume` reply** (8 B, little-endian, defined in `include/storage_proto.h`), sent once as soon as the hub connects to `storage.sock`: 241 242 | Offset | Size | Field | Value | 243 |---|---|---|---| 244 | 0 | 1 B | magic | `0xA8` (distinct from the message's `0xA6` and the record's `0xA7`) | 245 | 1 | 1 B | version | 1 | 246 | 2 | 1 B | type | `0x10` seq_resume | 247 | 3 | 1 B | has_last | 0 = storage holds nothing yet (a fresh hub starts at 0; a running hub keeps its counter); 1 = `seq` is valid | 248 | 4 | 4 B | seq | the last accepted `seq` (0 when `has_last` is 0) | 249 250 - No CRC: the local socket keeps each message whole and does not corrupt it in transit; the record's CRC guards the SD card. 251 252 **Sensor → hub message** (16 B, packed and little-endian, defined in `include/ipc.h`): 253 254 | Offset | Size | Field | Value | 255 |---|---|---|---| 256 | 0 | 1 B | magic | `0xA6` (distinct from the record's `0xA7`) | 257 | 1 | 1 B | version | 1 | 258 | 2 | 1 B | type | `0x01` DATA, `0x02` GAP (same values as `record_type`) | 259 | 3 | 1 B | sensor_id | 1 = light, 2 = soil (0 is not valid from a sensor) | 260 | 4 | 4 B | counter | sensor-side counter; GAP: first refused reading | 261 | 8 | 4 B | seq | 0 from the sensor; the hub stamps it | 262 | 12 | 4 B | value | DATA: raw count; GAP: refused-reading count | 263 264 - The hub rejects a message with a bad magic, version, type or sensor_id (`ipc_bad_message`). A message shorter than 16 B is rejected at `recv()`. 265 - **Decided:** hub → storage sends the 24 B record (see *Record* above), not this message. The hub stamps the µs timestamp (8 B), which does not fit in 16 B alongside the type, sensor, seq and value. Stamping in the hub also keeps a record's receive time correct while it waits in the hub queue during a storage outage. 266 267 ### How records are organized 268 269 - There is one segment file per UTC day: `/var/lib/plantpi/log-YYYYMMDD.bin`. 270 - At midnight, storage first flushes the records it is holding into the old day's file, then creates the new one. A record goes into the previous day's file only if it arrived between midnight and the flush thread's next pass (≤ 1 s). 271 - Records are appended in `seq` order. Only the current day's file is open for writing, so only its tail can ever need recovery. 272 - When a new segment is created, storage fsyncs the directory as well, so the new file cannot disappear after a power cut. 273 274 ### With what retention 275 276 - Segments are kept for **30 days** (today and the 29 days before it), about 63 MB. When a new day's segment is created, a segment is deleted only if **both** its date is before that window **and** it is not one of the newest 30 segments. The second rule means a clock that jumps years ahead can't wipe out the history: retention only ever trims beyond 30 files. Rollover and retention are skipped while the clock is unsynced (`retention_skipped`, logged once per unsynced spell). 277 - **Nothing inside the 30-day window is ever deleted to make room.** If the card fills before 30 days (**planned**; until then a full card shows as `storage_write_error` (or `fsync_error`) + `storage_degraded`, with the records kept in memory): 278 - Storage logs `storage_disk_full`. 279 - It refuses and counts new readings. 280 - It writes a GAP record once space is available again. 281 - **Planned:** a 64 KB reserve (checked with `statvfs`) is always kept free, so a GAP record can always be written. 282 283 This follows the project's policy: protect existing history, and make any unavoidable loss explicit. See *Failure-mode table → Storage (disk full)*. 284 285 ### How writes are batched and when data is flushed 286 287 - The **rx thread** reads records from `storage.sock` and appends them, as the raw 24 B it received, to one **pending buffer** (up to 1 MB, about 43,690 records) under a mutex. The same buffer is the batch in normal operation and the outage queue when flushes fail, because records stay in it until a flush succeeds. 288 - The **flush thread** wakes once a second and commits when either of these comes first: 289 - **N = 64 records** pending, or 290 - **T = 60 s** since the **oldest** pending record was added (each record keeps its own add time, so a record that arrived during a slow flush still meets the 62 s commit target). At about 1.02 records/s, T is normally the trigger, which gives about 61 records (≈1.5 KB) per batch and about 1,440 fsyncs/day. 291 - **N and T are run-time options:** `storage_main -n N -t T_SECONDS` (default 64 and 60 s; N up to the 43,690-record buffer, T up to a day), logged on `storage_start` as `batch_n` / `batch_t_s`. The (N, T) comparison in *Mechanism D* therefore runs on one build. 292 - **N is acted on at once:** between its 1 s passes, the flush thread sleeps on a condition variable rather than a plain timer. The append that makes a flush due by count wakes it, so the commit starts straight away, and N = 1 really is one fsync per record. T, rollover and retention are still checked on the 1 s pass. The wake happens only when a flush *becomes* due: after a failed flush the records stay pending, and the thread retries on its next 1 s pass instead of spinning on a broken card. 293 - **Commit sequence:** 294 1. Lock the mutex and copy every pending record out (nothing is removed yet). 295 2. Unlock. The lock is never held during I/O. 296 3. `write()` them. 297 4. `fsync()` the segment. 298 5. Lock, drop the committed records from the buffer, record the new committed offset, unlock. 299 - **On SIGTERM**, storage commits whatever is pending, then creates the clean-shutdown marker `clean_shutdown` and fsyncs the directory. The marker is written only if that final flush succeeded. 300 - **A record is committed once `fsync()` returns.** Before then, it may be lost but is never reported as stored. 301 - **If `write()` or `fsync()` fails:** 302 - The batch stays in memory and storage is marked degraded immediately. 303 - On the next cycle, storage truncates the file back to the last committed offset, then rewrites and fsyncs the batch, so no duplicate or partial records reach the log. 304 - While the disk is unavailable, records keep queueing in the pending buffer, up to 1 MB (about 11 h). Storage logs `storage_backlog` once at each of 50%, 75% and 90% going up, with the threshold and the fill (`percent=N pending=P`). 305 - When the buffer is full, storage refuses and counts new readings (`storage_degraded reason=queue_full`, once per full spell). The next accepted reading skips their `seq`s, so a GAP whose `seq` is the first refused reading and whose count is the number refused goes in just before it. The GAP is stamped with the time of the last reading storage accepted before the refusals. 306 307 See *Mechanism D* (batching, durability point and outage rows) and *Failure-mode table → Storage*. 308 309 ### What happens when the power dies mid-write 310 311 **Guarantee:** a power cut loses at most one unsynced batch (≤ 60 s), plus any backlog held in memory during a storage outage. It never leaves a corrupt record readable. 312 313 On every start, **recovery runs before `storage.sock` accepts any data**. This is the same path after a power cut and after a supervisor restart or `kill -9`. Storage first takes the one-listener lock (`storage.sock.lock`), so no second storage process can be recovering or appending at the same time. 314 315 1. If the clean-shutdown marker `clean_shutdown` is missing and at least one segment exists, log `unclean_shutdown` (a fresh install has nothing to recover, so it is not reported). A marker that is there is deleted and the directory fsynced at once, so it can't survive into a run that later crashes. 316 2. Check the **newest** segment's header (only the segment being appended to can have a damaged tail). If it is invalid or the file is shorter than 16 B, rename it to `.corrupt`, log `segment_corrupt`, and start a fresh segment. An earlier `.corrupt` copy of the same segment is never replaced: the next copy becomes `.2.corrupt`, then `.3.corrupt`, and so on. `.corrupt` files are evidence and are never deleted. Known limit: storage reads at most 128 directory names, so a directory holding more (about 90 `.corrupt` files beside 30 segments) stops storage at start with `storage_open_error` until old `.corrupt` files are cleared by hand. 317 3. Scan the records from the start of the segment. Stop at the **first** record that has any of these problems: 318 - bad magic, unknown `record_type` or wrong version 319 - CRC mismatch 320 - `seq` that does not increase 321 - a partial (fewer than 24 B) trailing record 322 4. `ftruncate()` the file at that offset, `fsync()` it, and log `recovery_event` with the bytes and records removed. 323 5. If the newest segment holds no records (header-only, or renamed `.corrupt`), read older segments, newest first, until one gives the last `seq` on disk. Each older segment is recovered the same way, and every one that is cut or renamed is logged too (`recovery_event` / `segment_corrupt`, with its name). 324 6. Open `storage.sock` and resume normal operation. 325 326 Records are fixed-size, so the scan is simple offset arithmetic. The target is under 1 s for a full day's segment. 327 328 See *Mechanism D → "Survive being unplugged" and "Restarts must not corrupt the log"*, and *Failure-mode table → Storage (corrupt tail)* and *Power*. 329 330 ## Constraints and substitutions 331 This section covers compute, storage and IPC. 1 # Sensor Pipeline: plan and status 2 3 The official plan for Green Thumb's sensor-side pipeline, from the I2C seam up to the 16 B message a sensor process sends to the hub and the 24 B record the hub sends to storage. That covers the BH1750 light-sensor driver and the shared pieces it relies on: sensor health tracking, the log line formatter, the sensor→hub message and the hub→storage record codec, plus the IPC client that carries the 16 B message over `hub.sock`. A new session should be able to read this file, plus `CLAUDE.md` and `DESIGN.md`, and pick up where work stopped without re-explanation. 4 5 Since 2026-10-26 the file also holds a second top-level part, *Mechanism D: storage*, with its own Goal, Code map, Decisions, Status, *Not done yet* and Log. So there are two Status sections: **Status** (the sensor pipeline and IPC, Steps 0–24) and **Status (Mechanism D)** (storage). **Update either Status section only at the end of the day, when asked.** 6 7 ## Context 8 - **Owner:** Lily (DESIGN.md → Ownership map: "Light sensor (driver and process)" and "IPC (data path)"). 9 - **Goal of this phase:** prove the sensor is *electrically alive* and *trustworthy* before it is connected to the data pipeline. That means the bus opens, the chip ACKs, reads decode, failures are retried and bounded, and a sensor that keeps failing is marked offline instead of silently producing nothing. Then pin the wire message the light process will send. 10 - **Goal of the IPC phase (Steps 10–24):** a reading leaves the sensor process and reaches a hub stand-in (`hub_listen`) over `hub.sock`. It survives the hub being killed and restarted (buffered, then resent in order, or covered by a GAP), and the client never blocks the 1 Hz sampling. 11 - **Hardware:** BH1750 on `/dev/i2c-1` at address `0x23` (ADDR pin low or floating). Continuous high-res mode at 1 lx/count; each conversion takes at most 180 ms. Lux = raw / 1.2. **Raw counts are stored, never lux.** 12 - **Sampling rate:** 1 Hz (DESIGN.md). The 1 Hz schedule belongs to the sampler, not the driver. 13 - **Rule from DESIGN.md's failure-mode table (Sensor (I2C) row):** retry 3× at 10 ms, then skip the sample. After 10 consecutive failures, mark the sensor offline and retry every 5 s. Log `i2c_read_error`, `sensor_offline` and `sensor_online`. 14 15 ## Design principle 16 - **Layered seam:** `src/i2c_bus.c` is the only file that makes I2C system calls. The driver talks to the bus only through `gt_i2c_ops` (`write` / `read` / `sleep_ms` / `close`). Tests swap in `tests/fake_i2c.h`, so every driver path, including injected NACKs and short reads, runs in WSL/CI with no hardware. 17 - **Logic stays separate from hardware** (CLAUDE.md): anything that can be pure logic (health tracking, message encoding) takes its inputs as arguments (`gt_status`, `now_ms`, bytes) and makes no system calls. 18 - **Each layer fails explicitly:** a failure returns a `gt_status` and leaves outputs untouched. No layer invents a value. 19 - **IPC seam (same idea as the I2C seam):** `src/ipc_sock.c` is the only file that makes **client-side** socket system calls (`socket`, `connect`, `send`, `close`). Servers make their own (see *Decisions*, PF-16). The IPC client (`src/ipc_client.c`) talks to the socket only through `gt_sock_ops` (`connect` / `send` / `disconnect` / `destroy`), with the current time passed in as `now_ms`. Tests swap in `tests/fake_sock.h`, so the backoff, ring and GAP logic all run in WSL/CI with no hub and no real waiting. 20 21 ### Code map 22 How the modules work together to carry a reading from sensor → IPC → hub → storage. It is a small public struct with no malloc. 100 - **Health input:** any non-`GT_OK` result from `gt_light_read` counts as one failure. The driver's 3 retries are already inside a single failed read. 101 - **Health output:** `gt_health_record` returns a transition event (`NONE` / `OFFLINE` / `ONLINE`) and the caller logs it. The tracker does no I/O. 102 - **Time is passed in** as `now_ms`, matching `gt_sampler_tick`, so tests need no clock. 103 - **Test ID prefixes:** `SHR` (sensor health record), `SHS` (sensor health should-read), `SHE` (sensor health event name), `LGF` (log format), `MSE` (message encode), `MSD` (message decode), `CRC` (CRC-32), `RCE` (record encode), `RCD` (record decode), `IFD` (IPC frame decode), `ICO` (IPC client open), `ICC` (IPC client close), `ICS` (IPC client send), `ICR` (IPC client reconnect), `IOV` (IPC client overflow), `IPL` (IPC loopback over a real socket). 104 - **Log ownership:** the light sensor's events (`i2c_read_error`, `sensor_offline`, `sensor_online`) are Lily's, as the light process's read-failure handling. The shared formatter (`gt_log_format`) has no owner in the Ownership map because every component uses it, so it counts as **Joint → Architecture integration**. Lily writes it first, as its first caller; give Lucas a heads-up so his components reuse it. 105 - **Log line:** ` [ key=value ...]`. The timestamp is µs since the Unix epoch, as a plain integer, the same unit as the on-disk record, so logs and records can be joined. The levels are `DEBUG` / `INFO` / `WARN` / `ERROR`. The light process logs `sensor_offline` as WARN and `sensor_online` as INFO. 106 - **Log sink: stderr** (decided 2026-10-27, PF-18). The formatter only fills a caller-provided buffer, and every process writes the finished `gt_log_format` line to stderr, as `storage_main` already does. Children inherit the supervisor's stderr, so under systemd every line lands in the journal. Each process still reads the wall clock for its own timestamps. A shared file sink was rejected (rotation becomes our problem), and so was sending lines to the monitor process (it waits on Mechanism E). 107 - **Hop 2 (hub→storage) carries the 24 B on-disk record** (decided 2026-10-23). The hub stamps `seq` and the µs timestamp, builds the record (CRC included), and storage checks it (amended 2026-10-26, PF-01: the timestamp is stamped on arrival, `seq` + CRC at send time; see *Hub contract (hop 2)*) with `gt_record_decode`, then appends it unchanged. There are two reasons. First, DESIGN.md already has the hub stamping the time and storage reading *records* from `storage.sock`. Second, a record that waits in the hub's 1024-record queue during a storage outage (up to about 17 min) keeps its real receive time. If storage stamped the time instead, the timestamp would be off by however long the record waited. 108 - **The hub's next `seq` after connecting to storage is max(own next, `seq_resume` + 1)** (decided 2026-10-26, PF-03). A freshly started hub has no counter, so it takes storage's reply + 1 (0 on an empty log). A running hub keeps its own counter, defined as 1 + the last `seq` whose `send()` succeeded, so records storage lost in a `kill -9` (unsynced, or still in the socket) leave a hole that storage turns into a GAP (`recovery_gap`). The alternative, always continuing from the reply, was rejected: it reuses the lost `seq`s, so the loss leaves no GAP and the hub's sent log holds duplicates, which breaks "no reading is lost silently" and the Evaluation plan's lost-readings formula. Only a loss where the hub restarts too (power cut) is shown by `unclean_shutdown` alone, which DESIGN.md's Power row already allows. Storage needed no change: its sequence guard already writes the GAP. This rule sets what PF-01 (when to stamp) and PF-02 (the sender's states) must support, and what `storage_faults.sh` checks (PF-04/05). 109 - **Hub contract for hop 2** (decided 2026-10-26, PF-01/PF-02): the hub stamps the time on arrival and `seq` + CRC at send; the socket seam gains `recv`; the sender waits for `seq_resume` (2 s deadline) before sending anything. See *Hub contract (hop 2)*. 110 - **Message magic is `0xA6`** (proposed), distinct from the on-disk record's `0xA7`, so a record can never be misread as a message. 111 - **Truncated messages are rejected at `recv()`,** which must return exactly `GT_MSG_SIZE`, not in decode. Decode keeps its fixed 16 B array. 112 - **Range checks stay in the hub:** decode doesn't check that light ≤ 65535. That is the hub's `reading_invalid` check. 113 - **Deferred:** `src/light_sensor_main.c` (open → sample → health → send) waited until the IPC client existed. The client was completed on 2026-10-24, so it is now the next item (see *Not done yet*). 114 - **`hub.sock` is AF_UNIX `SOCK_SEQPACKET`** (decided 2026-10-24). The kernel keeps message boundaries, so each `send()` is one whole 16 B message and each `recv()` returns exactly one message. A short message shows up as a short `recv()`, which is where DESIGN.md rejects it, and there are no partial sends to track. `SOCK_STREAM` would need frame reassembly and resync code in the hub. 115 - **`hub_listen` stands in for the hub on the Pi** (decided 2026-10-24) until `gt_hub_accept` and the hub process exist. It's a small tool (`src/hub_listen_main.c`, `make hub_listen`) that prints each decoded message and flags counter gaps. With it, the kill -9 / kill -STOP fault tests can run now. 116 - **The client never blocks the sampler:** every socket call is non-blocking, and `send` uses `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, so a dead hub returns `EPIPE` instead of raising SIGPIPE, which would kill the sensor process. 117 - **Time is passed in** (`now_ms` on `gt_ipc_client_send` / `_pump`), as with the health tracker, so the backoff tests need no clock and no sleeps. 118 - **Events are returned, not logged:** the client returns `GT_IPC_EV_DISCONNECT` / `_RECONNECT` / `_OVERFLOW` bit flags, and the caller logs `ipc_disconnect` / `ipc_reconnect` / `ipc_overflow`, the same pattern as `gt_health_record`. 119 - **`gt_ipc_client_open` doesn't connect.** A hub that isn't up yet is not an error (DESIGN.md, Mechanism E: processes tolerate unavailable peers at startup). The first attempt happens on the first send or pump. 120 - **GAP needs 2 free slots:** after an overflow, a new reading is accepted only when the ring can hold both the GAP and the reading. This keeps the order: old data, then the GAP, then new data. Otherwise the reading is refused and counted into the same gap. 121 - **Close drops the buffer:** `gt_ipc_client_close` sends nothing more. Readings still in the ring are lost, and that's documented, not silent. 122 - **Limitation (no app-level ack):** a message the kernel accepted but the hub never `recv()`d before dying is lost. The hub sees the jump in the counter as a `sensor_seq_gap`. 123 - **`gt_ipc_client_open_ops` is declared in `ipc_sock.h`, not `ipc.h`** (Step 11). `ipc_sock.h` includes `ipc.h`, so putting it in `ipc.h` would make the two headers include each other. `gt_light_open_bus` sits next to its seam in `light_sensor.h` for the same reason. 124 - **Ownership of the ctx:** once `ops` is non-NULL, the client owns the ctx and calls `destroy` exactly once, from `close` or straight away if the client can't be allocated. With NULL ops there's no `destroy` to call, so the caller keeps the ctx. 125 - **`send` drains, pushes, then drains again** (Step 18). Draining before the push sends older frames first, which can free the slot the new reading needs, so a reading isn't refused when the hub could already have taken the backlog. 126 - **Any send result other than OK or FULL counts as the hub gone** (Step 19): disconnect, report `GT_IPC_EV_DISCONNECT` and retry after the wait. Both failure paths (a failed connect and a lost hub) share `schedule_retry`, so the wait doubles the same way for each. 127 - **Order moved to fit the link** (decided 2026-10-24). Every test binary links every file in `src/`, so nothing in `src/` may call a function that doesn't exist yet. `gt_ipc_client_open` calls `gt_ipc_sock_linux`, so it moved from Step 16 to Step 22, and its tests ICO-03/04 moved from Step 15 to Step 21. ICC-03 needs `send` to leave a frame in the ring, so it moved from Step 17 to Step 18. 128 - **One listener per socket, enforced by a lock** (decided 2026-10-24). A process that listens on a socket (`hub_listen` now; the hub and storage later) first takes an `fcntl` write lock on `.lock` and holds it for its whole life. Only the lock holder may remove a leftover socket file and bind a new one; a second copy prints `already running` and exits without touching anything. The kernel drops the lock when the holder dies, `kill -9` included, so a crash never leaves a stale lock. This is safer than probing with `connect()`, which leaves a gap: two copies started together could both see the file as stale, and the second would take the first one's address. Closing *any* fd the process holds on the lock file releases the lock, so the file is opened in one place only. When the hub is written, this moves into a shared `src/` helper; testing it needs `fork()`, because a process never blocks on its own `fcntl` lock. 129 - **The socket seam is for clients; servers call the socket API directly** (decided 2026-10-27, PF-16). Clients (`gt_ipc_client`, and later the hub's hop-2 sender) go through `gt_sock_ops`, because their backoff, ring and resume logic is worth testing against a fake with no real waiting. Servers (`listen_sock.c`, `storage_server.c`, and later the hub's rx loop) call `socket` / `bind` / `listen` / `accept` / `recv` / `send` themselves and are tested over real sockets in a `/tmp` directory (LBD, SSV, and later the hub loopback). A server loop is mostly "wait in `poll()`, then hand the bytes on", which a real socket tests well. A server-side seam with its own fake was rejected: it would add an ops table and a second fake to test very little logic. 130 131 ## Wire format: sensor → hub message (16 B, little-endian, encoded byte by byte) 132 | Off | Size | Field | Value | 133 |---|---|---|---| 134 | 0 | 1 | magic | `GT_MSG_MAGIC` = `0xA6` | 135 | 1 | 1 | version | `GT_MSG_VERSION` = 1 | 136 | 2 | 1 | type | `GT_MSG_DATA` = 1, `GT_MSG_GAP` = 2 (same values as `gt_rec_type`) | 137 | 3 | 1 | sensor_id | 1 light, 2 soil (0 = all is not valid on hop 1) | 138 | 4 | 4 | counter | sensor-side counter (for a GAP: the first refused counter) | 139 | 8 | 4 | seq | 0 from the sensor; the hub stamps it | 140 | 12 | 4 | value | DATA: raw count; GAP: refused-reading count | 141 142 Magic and version are written by encode and checked by decode. They are not `gt_msg` fields; `type` becomes one. 143 144 ## Wire format: hub → storage record (24 B) 145 Hop 2 sends the on-disk record exactly as DESIGN.md *In what format → Record* lays it out: magic `0xA7`, type, version, sensor_id, seq (u32 at 4), timestamp (u64 µs at 8), value (u32 at 16) and CRC-32 over bytes 0–19 (at 20). `gt_record` and the codec live in `include/log_record.h`. **Watch the header order:** the record goes magic, **type, version**, sensor_id, while the message goes magic, **version, type**, sensor_id. Don't copy the message encoder without swapping those two bytes. Unlike the message, a GAP record may use sensor_id 0 (all). 146 147 ## Hub contract (hop 2): stamping, numbering and the sender 148 Decided 2026-10-26 to settle PF-01 and PF-02 (Pipeline-Findings.md) before any hub code exists. It builds on the PF-03 numbering rule in *Decisions*. Nothing here is built yet. `include/hub.h` and `include/ipc_sock.h` change to match when the hub steps start, test first. 149 150 **Why it changes (PF-01):** a hub that has just started doesn't know its next `seq` until storage's `seq_resume` reply arrives. Storage may be down or still recovering, and Mechanism E says the hub must keep running anyway. So the hub can't finish a record (`seq` + CRC) when the sensor message arrives. It finishes it when it sends it. 151 152 ### Who stamps what, and when 153 | Field | Set by | When | Why | 154 |---|---|---|---| 155 | `type`, `sensor_id`, `value` | `gt_hub_accept` | message arrives | copied from the checked message | 156 | `timestamp_us` | `gt_hub_accept` (`now_us` passed in) | message arrives | keeps the real receive time while the record waits in the queue (the 2026-10-23 reason still holds) | 157 | `seq` | the hop-2 sender | just before `send()` | only the sender knows the next `seq` (max rule) | 158 | CRC-32 | `gt_record_encode`, called by the sender | just before `send()` | the CRC covers `seq`, so it can't be computed earlier | 159 160 - **`gt_hub_accept`'s new contract:** validate, range-check and de-duplicate one `gt_msg`. On `GT_OK`, fill `*out` with type, sensor, value and `timestamp_us = now_us`, and leave `seq` at 0. The hub plan adds the event flags it returns (`reading_invalid`, `ipc_duplicate`, `sensor_seq_gap`). 688	## Goal
689	Every reading the hub forwards reaches the microSD card in a form that survives a power cut, a `kill -9` or a full disk queue without a corrupt record ever being readable, and without a reading being lost silently (DESIGN.md Mechanism D). Built on branch `Menu-Mechanism-D`, test first throughout: each step's tests were written and seen failing before the code.
690	
691	## Code map

711	## Decisions (Mechanism D)
712	- **One pending buffer** (2026-10-26). The 64-record batch and the 1 MB outage queue are the same buffer: records stay in it until a flush succeeds. A flush writes everything pending.
713	- **Raw bytes are stored.** The pending buffer keeps the 24 B exactly as received and checked by `gt_record_decode`; a flush writes them unchanged, with no second encode.
714	- **Each pending record keeps its add time**, so a record that arrives during a slow flush is still flushed within the 62 s commit-latency target (about 350 KB at full capacity). The first version restarted the clock at commit; it was changed to stay inside the Evaluation plan.
715	- **The mutex lives inside `gt_storage`** and is never held during file I/O. `handle`, `committed_offset` and `degraded` belong to the one flushing thread.
716	- **Segment names use integer date maths, not `gmtime_r`:** on 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS `time_t` is 32 bits and `gmtime_r` fails after January 2038. Checked against Python for every day 1970–2100.
717	- **Recovery repairs only the newest segment**; if it holds no records, older segments are read for the last `seq`.
718	- **A clock behind the log keeps appending** to the newest segment instead of creating an earlier-dated one.
719	- **The shutdown is its own function** (`gt_storage_shutdown`), separate from `close`, so a failed final flush is reported and never followed by a marker. `close` writes nothing.
720	- **`unclean_shutdown` only when segments exist:** a fresh install is not a crash.
721	- **Backlog and full-buffer events:** `storage_backlog` once per threshold crossing (50/75/90%), `storage_degraded reason=queue_full` once per full spell. The GAP for refused readings comes for free from the sequence guard: refusing leaves the last accepted `seq` alone, so the next reading skips the refused ones.
722	- **Retention deletes only outside the window and beyond the newest 30**, so a clock that jumps forward can't wipe the history. Rollover while degraded first cuts the old segment's torn tail (Step 11b).
723	- **Lock before open:** storage takes `storage.sock.lock` before recovery, so two storage processes can never touch one segment.
724	- **`seq_resume` carries the last *accepted* `seq`**, not the last committed (DESIGN.md corrected).
725	- **The rx loop and flush thread live in the library**, so the loop is tested over a real socket (SSV) and one flush pass with the fake (FTK); `storage_main` only wires them up. On stop, frames already in the socket are still accepted.
726	- **Verifier coverage rule:** after `seq` *s* the next must be *s* + 1, unless the previous record is a GAP and the next equals `GAP.seq + GAP.value`.
727	- **The sent check compares ranges, not counts** (2026-10-27, PF-12). Within one hub run the sent `seq`s are one unbroken range A..B, and a passing report already guarantees every `seq` from its first to its last is stored or GAP-covered. So `gt_verify_sent` only compares the two ranges:
728	  - lost = the sent `seq`s outside the log's range;
729	  - a `seq` after B fails as `seq_not_sent`;
730	  - `seq`s before A (earlier runs) are allowed.
731	
732	  Counting `data + gap_readings` was rejected. It only worked because `storage_feed` never sends a GAP: a hub GAP has its own `seq`, and its value counts refused readings that never got one, so the sum would be wrong once the hub exists. A per-`seq` sent log was rejected as unnecessary, since a range says the same.
733	- **Rollover flushes the old day first** (2026-10-26, PF-06). `gt_storage_rollover` flushes pending records into the old segment before it creates the new one, so a day's records stay in that day's file. A record that arrives between midnight and the flusher's next 1 s pass still counts as the old day's. Splitting each batch by each record's own day was rejected: it is exact, but needs a much larger change to the flush and the pending buffer. If the pre-flush fails, the existing degraded path cuts the old tail and the records go into the new segment. SRO-11, SRO-12 and FTK-05 were changed with approval, because they asserted the old behaviour.
734	- **A storage-made GAP carries the last accepted record's time** (2026-10-26, PF-07). That is the earliest the gap could have started, and the next record marks its end, so the gap's length is kept. Recovery reports the newest record's time (`last_timestamp_us` in the scan, the report and the open info), so a GAP found after a `kill -9` gets it too. `gt_seq_gap_record` takes it as a new argument. Keeping the "time storage found out" was rejected: start and end were the same, so the length was lost. SQG-07 and SFL-03 were changed with approval, because they asserted the old time.
735	- **Commits are timed inside storage and logged by the caller** (2026-10-27, PF-08). An optional monotonic clock (`gt_storage_set_clock`) times every commit (`commit_us`) and its fsync alone (`fsync_us`), including the rollover pre-flush and the shutdown flush. Storage keeps returning events as flags with no I/O, so the numbers go into `gt_storage_stats`. `gt_storage_log_commit` turns them into `storage_commit` (INFO) and `fsync_slow` (WARN, over 1 s), called once per flush-thread pass and around the shutdown. Timing the whole flush in the flush thread was rejected: it mixes write and fsync and misses two of the three commit paths. fsync p50/p99 are computed offline from the log. FTK-02 was changed with approval: it asserted a healthy flush logs nothing.
736	- **Log lines carry their facts** (2026-10-27, PF-14). `storage_backlog` has `percent=N pending=P`, logged by `gt_storage_log_rx_events` because event flags can't carry numbers. `storage_stop` has `segment=… last_seq=…`. Open reports every older segment that the walk back cut or renamed: up to 8 by name, any more counted.
737	- **`.corrupt` files are kept, never replaced** (2026-10-27, PF-20). A second copy of the same segment gets `<name>.2.corrupt` and so on. Retention still never deletes them, so the 128-name listing limit is a documented known limit rather than a fix. `segment_create_error` is logged once per failure spell.
738	- **An empty log waits for the clock** (2026-10-27, PF-20). `storage_main` waits up to 120 s for `clock_synced` before open names the first segment (`clock_wait`, `clock_wait_done`), so an unsynced Pi doesn't start `log-19700101.bin`. Deferring segment creation inside the library was rejected: it is exact, but needs a "no active segment" state across open, flush and rollover. A log that already holds a segment never waits.
739	- **The clock's unsynced period is logged by the flush thread** (2026-10-27, PF-13). It already gets `clock_synced` and the monotonic `now_ms` on every pass, so it logs `clock_unsynced` once per spell and `clock_synced unsynced_ms=N` when the spell ends.
740	- **Storage's heartbeat is sent by the rx thread** (proposed 2026-10-27, PF-10; **pending Lucas**, who owns the heartbeat). The flush thread can sit in a stalled `fsync()` for seconds, so a heartbeat sent from it would stop exactly when the supervisor most needs to tell "slow" from "hung". The rx thread never touches the disk. DESIGN.md's diagram now matches its `fsync_slow` row. What building it needs, once `sup.sock` exists:
741	  - `gt_storage_serve`'s `poll()` takes a 1000 ms timeout instead of `-1`, so the beat goes out even when the hub is quiet.
742	  - The beat carries "flush in progress since t" and the committed-record count, so `gt_storage_stats` gains the time the current flush started.
743	  - Nothing is built until then.
744	- **N and T are run-time options, and an append wakes the flusher** (2026-10-27, PF-11). `storage_main -n N -t T_SECONDS` sets them through `gt_storage_set_batch` → `gt_pending_set_limits` (the `#define`s stay as the defaults). Between its 1 s passes, the flush thread waits in `gt_storage_wait_due` on a condition variable (on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux), so the append that makes a flush due starts the commit at once.
745	  - **The signal fires only when a flush *becomes* due,** and each wait uses it up. Firing "while due" was rejected: after a failed flush the records stay pending, so the flusher would spin retrying a broken card instead of waiting for its 1 s pass (SWT-03).
746	  - **`storage_main` calls `gt_storage_wake` after the rx loop returns,** because a signal handler can't safely call `pthread_cond_signal`.
747	  - **Rejected:** keeping the 1 s poll and rewording DESIGN.md (then N = 1 would mean "flush every second"), and rebuilding with `-D` for each point.
748	- **Test ID prefixes:** `SGH` segment header, `RSC` recovery scan, `PND` pending buffer, `SQG` sequence guard, `SRV` storage recover, `SNM` segment name, `SOP` open, `SAP` append, `SFL` flush, `SFE` flush errors, `SCL` shutdown, `SBL` backlog, `SRO` rollover, `SLB` real-file loopback, `LCK` listen lock, `LBD` listen bind, `RSE` / `RSD` resume encode / decode, `SRX` rx frames, `SEV` event names, `FTK` flusher tick (incl. commit and clock logging), `SSV` serve loopback, `VFY` verifier, `NSQ` next seq (`gt_next_seq`, PF-03), `SLE` storage log events (PF-14), `VSR` verifier sent range (PF-12), `PNL` pending limits, `SBT` storage batch settings, `SWT` storage wait / wake (PF-11).

773	## Verification (Mechanism D)
774	- **Every step:** `make test && make asan && make memcheck` in WSL; GitHub CI runs the same.
775	- **The real process** (WSL), with `D=$(mktemp -d); S=$D/storage.sock`:
776	  1. `build/storage_main $D/log $S`: `storage_start ... created=1 last_seq=none`.
777	  2. A second copy prints `already running`.
778	  3. `build/storage_feed $S 200 0`: `sending from 0`, `seq 0..199`.
779	  4. Ctrl-C: `storage_stop clean=1 committed=200`.
780	  5. Restart + feed: no `unclean_shutdown`, the reply continues at 199.
781	  6. Feed at 10 Hz and `kill -9` storage mid-feed.
782	  7. Restart: `unclean_shutdown` and `recovery_event`; the reply is the last committed `seq`.
783	- **Fault rounds:** `tools/storage_faults.sh sigterm 20` and `tools/storage_faults.sh kill9 50`. Target: `0 failed checks`.
784	  - **One feed for the whole run:** `storage_feed -r` acts as a hub that keeps running while storage restarts, so a `kill -9` loss must show up as a GAP (PF-03), not as reused `seq`s.
785	  - **Each round:**
786	    1. Start storage and wait for its `storage_start` line. The socket file can't be trusted, because a `kill -9` leaves the old one behind.
787	    2. Check that it did *not* log `unclean_shutdown`, since every start follows a clean stop.
788	    3. Check that the feed's `seq_resume` reply equals the last `seq` the verifier saw.
789	    4. Stop storage: SIGTERM after a random 0.1–0.9 s, or `kill -9` after a random 1.0–2.9 s. The flusher commits once a second, so an earlier kill would never see a commit and every loss would hit the empty-log case, where storage writes no GAP.
790	    5. **`kill9` only, a recovery pass (PF-05):** pause the feed (`SIGSTOP`), start storage so it recovers (it must log `unclean_shutdown`), then SIGTERM it.
791	    6. `log_verify` must pass, and the log may not cover more `seq`s than the feed has sent. In `sigterm` mode it must hold no GAP.
792	  - **Settle and the final check:** after the last round, start storage once more so the last hole gets its GAP. Then stop the feed, which reports `sent N records, seq A..B`, and stop storage. The check is the Evaluation plan's formula, run as `log_verify --sent A..B` (PF-12): every `seq` in A..B is committed or GAP-covered and nothing past B is stored, i.e. sent − committed − GAP-covered = 0 (`lost=0`). The script also checks N = B − A + 1 (no `seq` reused) and that the log starts at A, since this run's log starts empty.
793	  - **Negative control (2026-10-26):** a scratch build of the feed that always continued from the reply + 1 passed every per-round check in `kill9 5`, but failed the final check ("1600 records in 0..1165").
794	- **(N, T) settings (PF-11):** `build/storage_main -n 1 -t 1 $D/log $S` with `build/storage_feed $S 50 10`. `storage_start` shows `batch_n=1 batch_t_s=1`, and the log holds about 50 `storage_commit records=1` lines: one fsync per record, not one per second.
795	- **Power pulls (on the Pi, by hand, 20 times):**
796	  1. Image the SD card first, so a damaged card can be restored.
797	  2. Start `storage_main /var/lib/plantpi /run/plantpi/storage.sock` and `storage_feed /run/plantpi/storage.sock 100000 50`.
798	  3. Pull the USB-C cable at a random moment. Note the time since the last `storage_start` or commit, so the results can say how many pulls really landed mid-batch.
799	  4. Boot, start `storage_main` (expect `unclean_shutdown`, maybe `recovery_event`), stop it, then run `log_verify /var/lib/plantpi`.
800	  5. Target: `log_verify` passes every time; loss ≤ one unsynced batch (the `seq_resume` gap to the feed's last sent `seq` is ≤ 64 records or 60 s).
801	
802	## Not done yet (Mechanism D)
803	- **Disk full and read-only file system:** `ENOSPC`, the 64 KB `statvfs` reserve, and `EROFS` (`storage_disk_full`, `storage_readonly`). Each needs a "disk full" status out of the file seam first.
804	- **The hub side of hop 2:** reading `seq_resume` and picking the next `seq` by the max rule (Decisions, PF-03), and the 1024-record queue (see *Not done yet* above).
805	- **The heartbeat to `sup.sock`:** Mechanism E. Proposed to come from the rx thread (*Decisions*, PF-10, pending Lucas).
806	- **The clock wait, on the Pi:** on an empty log `storage_main` now waits up to 120 s for the clock (PF-20), but WSL's clock is always synced, so the wait has not been seen running. Check it on the Pi with the network unplugged.
807	- **On-Pi runs:** the fault rounds and power pulls above.
808	
809	## Log (Mechanism D)
810	- **2026-10-26:** Mechanism D planned and built in one day on `Menu-Mechanism-D`: Steps 1–13b above, 308 tests across 42 binaries, all green under `make test`, `make asan` and `make memcheck` in WSL and in CI. DESIGN.md brought in line with what was built (pending buffer, retention rule, recovery order, lock before open, `seq_resume` format and its last-accepted `seq`, `storage.sock` as `SOCK_SEQPACKET`, new log events).
811	
812	  Surprises:
813	  - `gmtime_r` can't name a segment after 2038 on 32-bit Pi OS, so dates are computed with integer arithmetic.
814	  - `renameat` is declared in `<stdio.h>`; the build would have failed in WSL without it.
815	  - GitHub CI (gcc) failed on `-Wformat-truncation` in a test's clean-up path that clang on the Mac accepted; fixed by deleting files with `unlinkat` instead of building paths. Two other spots were hardened the same way (`memcpy` of a measured length in `list`; an unsigned comparison in SAP's helper).
816	  - SOP-01 first checked durability with `fake_fs_power_cut()` and then closed storage, which a real power cut can't follow; it now checks the fake's synced copy.
817	  - Step 10's events changed what SAP-08/09 expected (`QUEUE_FULL` on the first refusal, `BACKLOG` while filling); both were updated with approval to expect the exact events.
818	  - A rollover while degraded would have stranded torn bytes in yesterday's segment, which recovery never revisits; found while writing Step 11 and fixed test-first as Step 11b.
819	  - macOS has no `SOCK_SEQPACKET` for local sockets, no `SOCK_CLOEXEC` / `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, and its leak checker hangs on tests that `fork()`; the socket tests (LBD, SSV) run only on Linux.
820	
821	  Next: run `storage_faults.sh` in WSL and the power pulls on the Pi, then the hub's hop-2 sender (or Mechanism E).

- **Expected state:** green straight away, since close already exists. This step checks it.

### Step 18: send, connected path (red → green)
- **New `tests/test_ipc_send.c`:**
  - ICS-01 the first send connects, then sends bytes equal to `gt_msg_encode`
  - ICS-02 several sends arrive in order
  - ICS-03 a bad type or sensor 0 → `GT_ERR_INVAL`, nothing queued or sent
  - ICS-04 NULL client or msg → `GT_ERR_INVAL`
  - ICS-05 `EAGAIN` keeps the frame, stays connected, no event
  - ICS-06 the next send flushes the held frame, then the new one
- **Add to `tests/test_ipc_close.c`:** ICC-03, closing with a frame buffered (left by one `EAGAIN`) sends nothing, Valgrind clean.
- **Edit `src/ipc_client.c`:**
  - the static `ring_push`
  - the static `drain`, connected path only
  - `gt_ipc_client_send`, which drains, pushes, then drains again

  Two temporary pieces stood in until Step 19: a single connect attempt with no backoff, and `(void)now_ms;` to keep `-Werror` quiet about the unused parameter.
- **Done when:** all three targets pass, ICS 6/6 and ICC 3/3.

### Step 19: reconnect and backoff (red → green)
- **New `tests/test_ipc_reconnect.c`:**
  - ICR-01 a failed connect → buffered, `GT_OK`, no event
  - ICR-02 attempts at 0/100/300/700/1500/3100 ms, never early
  - ICR-03 the wait caps at 2000 ms
  - ICR-04 a successful connect resets the wait to 100 ms
  - ICR-05 a gone peer → DISCONNECT once, frame kept, retry at +100 ms
  - ICR-06 reconnect → RECONNECT, ring drains oldest first
  - ICR-07 the first clean connect → no RECONNECT
  - ICR-08 `pump` reconnects and drains with no new message
- **Edit `src/ipc_client.c`:**
  - the static `schedule_retry`: the next attempt is now + the wait, the wait doubles up to 2000 ms, and the trouble is marked
  - the static `try_connect`: no attempt before the retry is due; on success the wait resets to 100 ms, and `RECONNECT` is reported only after trouble
  - `drain` uses `try_connect`; a send result of `GT_ERR_IO` disconnects, reports `DISCONNECT` and schedules a retry
  - `gt_ipc_client_send` collects events in a local and writes them out once (this removed the Step 18 temporaries)
  - `gt_ipc_client_pump`
- **Done when:** all three targets pass, ICR 8/8.

### Step 20: overflow and GAP (red → green)
- **New `tests/test_ipc_overflow.c`:**
  - IOV-01 64 readings buffered OK, the 65th → `GT_ERR_FULL` + OVERFLOW
  - IOV-02 OVERFLOW fires once per run, and `refused` counts every reading
  - IOV-03 the drain order is 64 data, then the GAP (first counter, count), then the new reading
  - IOV-04 with only 1 free slot, the new reading is refused into the same gap
  - IOV-05 a second overflow gives a second, separate GAP
- **Edit `src/ipc_client.c`:**
  - the static `enqueue_reading`: the overflow/refuse path. `send` calls it in place of `ring_push`.
  - the static `push_gap`, called from `enqueue_reading` once a pending gap has 2 free slots
  - `gt_ipc_client_stats`

  Each new static was wired in by the same write that added it, because `-Werror` makes an unused static a build error for every binary.
- **Done when:** all three targets pass, IOV 5/5.

### Step 21: loopback tests over a real socket (red)
- **New `tests/test_ipc_loopback.c`:** a real `SOCK_SEQPACKET` socket in a `mkdtemp` directory under `/tmp` (Windows-mounted drives in WSL2 don't reliably support socket files). `now_ms` is passed in, so the tests never sleep. Nothing blocks either: the listener is `SOCK_NONBLOCK` and every `recv` uses `MSG_DONTWAIT`, so a missing message is a FAIL line, not a hang. A small fixture comes in with IPL-01: the `loopback` struct plus `loopback_init`, `make_listener`, `recv_frame` and `loopback_cleanup`.
  - IPL-01 the listener receives 16 B, which frame-decodes to the same message
  - IPL-02 no listener (`ENOENT`) → buffered; once the listener appears → drained in order, with RECONNECT
  - IPL-03 the hub's connection and listener both close → DISCONNECT, no SIGPIPE crash (SIGPIPE is deliberately left at its default), frame kept; the retry finds no listener and stays quiet
  - IPL-04 light and soil clients share one listener, each stream in counter order
  - IPL-05 a raw 15 B packet arrives as 15 B and is rejected, `out` untouched; a 16 B packet sent after it arrives as exactly 16 (proves SEQPACKET keeps message boundaries)
- **Add to `tests/test_ipc_open.c`** (moved from Step 15):
  - ICO-03 `open(path)` with NULL, `""` or a 108 B path (the `sun_path` limit) → NULL
  - ICO-04 `open(path)` on a socket that doesn't exist still returns a handle, and its first `pump` is quiet (`GT_OK`, no event)

## Decisions (Mechanism D)
- **One pending buffer** (2026-10-26). The 64-record batch and the 1 MB outage queue are the same buffer: records stay in it until a flush succeeds. A flush writes everything pending.
- **Raw bytes are stored.** The pending buffer keeps the 24 B exactly as received and checked by `gt_record_decode`; a flush writes them unchanged, with no second encode.
- **Each pending record keeps its add time**, so a record that arrives during a slow flush is still flushed within the 62 s commit-latency target (about 350 KB at full capacity). The first version restarted the clock at commit; it was changed to stay inside the Evaluation plan.
- **The mutex lives inside `gt_storage`** and is never held during file I/O. `handle`, `committed_offset` and `degraded` belong to the one flushing thread.
- **Segment names use integer date maths, not `gmtime_r`:** on 32-bit Raspberry Pi OS `time_t` is 32 bits and `gmtime_r` fails after January 2038. Checked against Python for every day 1970–2100.
- **Recovery repairs only the newest segment**; if it holds no records, older segments are read for the last `seq`.
- **A clock behind the log keeps appending** to the newest segment instead of creating an earlier-dated one.
- **The shutdown is its own function** (`gt_storage_shutdown`), separate from `close`, so a failed final flush is reported and never followed by a marker. `close` writes nothing.
- **`unclean_shutdown` only when segments exist:** a fresh install is not a crash.
- **Backlog and full-buffer events:** `storage_backlog` once per threshold crossing (50/75/90%), `storage_degraded reason=queue_full` once per full spell. The GAP for refused readings comes for free from the sequence guard: refusing leaves the last accepted `seq` alone, so the next reading skips the refused ones.
- **Retention deletes only outside the window and beyond the newest 30**, so a clock that jumps forward can't wipe the history. Rollover while degraded first cuts the old segment's torn tail (Step 11b).
- **Lock before open:** storage takes `storage.sock.lock` before recovery, so two storage processes can never touch one segment.
- **`seq_resume` carries the last *accepted* `seq`**, not the last committed (DESIGN.md corrected).
- **The rx loop and flush thread live in the library**, so the loop is tested over a real socket (SSV) and one flush pass with the fake (FTK); `storage_main` only wires them up. On stop, frames already in the socket are still accepted.
- **Verifier coverage rule:** after `seq` *s* the next must be *s* + 1, unless the previous record is a GAP and the next equals `GAP.seq + GAP.value`.
- **The sent check compares ranges, not counts** (2026-10-27, PF-12). Within one hub run the sent `seq`s are one unbroken range A..B, and a passing report already guarantees every `seq` from its first to its last is stored or GAP-covered. So `gt_verify_sent` only compares the two ranges:
  - lost = the sent `seq`s outside the log's range;
  - a `seq` after B fails as `seq_not_sent`;
  - `seq`s before A (earlier runs) are allowed.

  Counting `data + gap_readings` was rejected. It only worked because `storage_feed` never sends a GAP: a hub GAP has its own `seq`, and its value counts refused readings that never got one, so the sum would be wrong once the hub exists. A per-`seq` sent log was rejected as unnecessary, since a range says the same.
- **Rollover flushes the old day first** (2026-10-26, PF-06). `gt_storage_rollover` flushes pending records into the old segment before it creates the new one, so a day's records stay in that day's file. A record that arrives between midnight and the flusher's next 1 s pass still counts as the old day's. Splitting each batch by each record's own day was rejected: it is exact, but needs a much larger change to the flush and the pending buffer. If the pre-flush fails, the existing degraded path cuts the old tail and the records go into the new segment. SRO-11, SRO-12 and FTK-05 were changed with approval, because they asserted the old behaviour.
- **A storage-made GAP carries the last accepted record's time** (2026-10-26, PF-07). That is the earliest the gap could have started, and the next record marks its end, so the gap's length is kept. Recovery reports the newest record's time (`last_timestamp_us` in the scan, the report and the open info), so a GAP found after a `kill -9` gets it too. `gt_seq_gap_record` takes it as a new argument. Keeping the "time storage found out" was rejected: start and end were the same, so the length was lost. SQG-07 and SFL-03 were changed with approval, because they asserted the old time.
- **Commits are timed inside storage and logged by the caller** (2026-10-27, PF-08). An optional monotonic clock (`gt_storage_set_clock`) times every commit (`commit_us`) and its fsync alone (`fsync_us`), including the rollover pre-flush and the shutdown flush. Storage keeps returning events as flags with no I/O, so the numbers go into `gt_storage_stats`. `gt_storage_log_commit` turns them into `storage_commit` (INFO) and `fsync_slow` (WARN, over 1 s), called once per flush-thread pass and around the shutdown. Timing the whole flush in the flush thread was rejected: it mixes write and fsync and misses two of the three commit paths. fsync p50/p99 are computed offline from the log. FTK-02 was changed with approval: it asserted a healthy flush logs nothing.
- **Log lines carry their facts** (2026-10-27, PF-14). `storage_backlog` has `percent=N pending=P`, logged by `gt_storage_log_rx_events` because event flags can't carry numbers. `storage_stop` has `segment=… last_seq=…`. Open reports every older segment that the walk back cut or renamed: up to 8 by name, any more counted.
- **`.corrupt` files are kept, never replaced** (2026-10-27, PF-20). A second copy of the same segment gets `<name>.2.corrupt` and so on. Retention still never deletes them, so the 128-name listing limit is a documented known limit rather than a fix. `segment_create_error` is logged once per failure spell.
- **An empty log waits for the clock** (2026-10-27, PF-20). `storage_main` waits up to 120 s for `clock_synced` before open names the first segment (`clock_wait`, `clock_wait_done`), so an unsynced Pi doesn't start `log-19700101.bin`. Deferring segment creation inside the library was rejected: it is exact, but needs a "no active segment" state across open, flush and rollover. A log that already holds a segment never waits.
- **The clock's unsynced period is logged by the flush thread** (2026-10-27, PF-13). It already gets `clock_synced` and the monotonic `now_ms` on every pass, so it logs `clock_unsynced` once per spell and `clock_synced unsynced_ms=N` when the spell ends.
- **Storage's heartbeat is sent by the rx thread** (proposed 2026-10-27, PF-10; **pending Lucas**, who owns the heartbeat). The flush thread can sit in a stalled `fsync()` for seconds, so a heartbeat sent from it would stop exactly when the supervisor most needs to tell "slow" from "hung". The rx thread never touches the disk. DESIGN.md's diagram now matches its `fsync_slow` row. What building it needs, once `sup.sock` exists:
  - `gt_storage_serve`'s `poll()` takes a 1000 ms timeout instead of `-1`, so the beat goes out even when the hub is quiet.
  - The beat carries "flush in progress since t" and the committed-record count, so `gt_storage_stats` gains the time the current flush started.
  - Nothing is built until then.
- **N and T are run-time options, and an append wakes the flusher** (2026-10-27, PF-11). `storage_main -n N -t T_SECONDS` sets them through `gt_storage_set_batch` → `gt_pending_set_limits` (the `#define`s stay as the defaults). Between its 1 s passes, the flush thread waits in `gt_storage_wait_due` on a condition variable (on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux), so the append that makes a flush due starts the commit at once.
  - **The signal fires only when a flush *becomes* due,** and each wait uses it up. Firing "while due" was rejected: after a failed flush the records stay pending, so the flusher would spin retrying a broken card instead of waiting for its 1 s pass (SWT-03).
  - **`storage_main` calls `gt_storage_wake` after the rx loop returns,** because a signal handler can't safely call `pthread_cond_signal`.
  - **Rejected:** keeping the 1 s poll and rewording DESIGN.md (then N = 1 would mean "flush every second"), and rebuilding with `-D` for each point.
- **Test ID prefixes:** `SGH` segment header, `RSC` recovery scan, `PND` pending buffer, `SQG` sequence guard, `SRV` storage recover, `SNM` segment name, `SOP` open, `SAP` append, `SFL` flush, `SFE` flush errors, `SCL` shutdown, `SBL` backlog, `SRO` rollover, `SLB` real-file loopback, `LCK` listen lock, `LBD` listen bind, `RSE` / `RSD` resume encode / decode, `SRX` rx frames, `SEV` event names, `FTK` flusher tick (incl. commit and clock logging), `SSV` serve loopback, `VFY` verifier, `NSQ` next seq (`gt_next_seq`, PF-03), `SLE` storage log events (PF-14), `VSR` verifier sent range (PF-12), `PNL` pending limits, `SBT` storage batch settings, `SWT` storage wait / wake (PF-11).

## Status (Mechanism D)
| Step | What | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Segment header codec | ✅ SGH 8/8 (121 tests, 20 binaries) |
| 2 | Recovery scan | ✅ RSC 9/9 (130, 21) |

| — | 20 power pulls on the Pi | ☐ Not run |

## Verification (Mechanism D)
- **Every step:** `make test && make asan && make memcheck` in WSL; GitHub CI runs the same.
- **The real process** (WSL), with `D=$(mktemp -d); S=$D/storage.sock`:
  1. `build/storage_main $D/log $S`: `storage_start ... created=1 last_seq=none`.
  2. A second copy prints `already running`.
  3. `build/storage_feed $S 200 0`: `sending from 0`, `seq 0..199`.
  4. Ctrl-C: `storage_stop clean=1 committed=200`.
  5. Restart + feed: no `unclean_shutdown`, the reply continues at 199.
  6. Feed at 10 Hz and `kill -9` storage mid-feed.
  7. Restart: `unclean_shutdown` and `recovery_event`; the reply is the last committed `seq`.
- **Fault rounds:** `tools/storage_faults.sh sigterm 20` and `tools/storage_faults.sh kill9 50`. Target: `0 failed checks`.
  - **One feed for the whole run:** `storage_feed -r` acts as a hub that keeps running while storage restarts, so a `kill -9` loss must show up as a GAP (PF-03), not as reused `seq`s.
  - **Each round:**
    1. Start storage and wait for its `storage_start` line. The socket file can't be trusted, because a `kill -9` leaves the old one behind.
    2. Check that it did *not* log `unclean_shutdown`, since every start follows a clean stop.
    3. Check that the feed's `seq_resume` reply equals the last `seq` the verifier saw.
    4. Stop storage: SIGTERM after a random 0.1–0.9 s, or `kill -9` after a random 1.0–2.9 s. The flusher commits once a second, so an earlier kill would never see a commit and every loss would hit the empty-log case, where storage writes no GAP.
    5. **`kill9` only, a recovery pass (PF-05):** pause the feed (`SIGSTOP`), start storage so it recovers (it must log `unclean_shutdown`), then SIGTERM it.
    6. `log_verify` must pass, and the log may not cover more `seq`s than the feed has sent. In `sigterm` mode it must hold no GAP.
  - **Settle and the final check:** after the last round, start storage once more so the last hole gets its GAP. Then stop the feed, which reports `sent N records, seq A..B`, and stop storage. The check is the Evaluation plan's formula, run as `log_verify --sent A..B` (PF-12): every `seq` in A..B is committed or GAP-covered and nothing past B is stored, i.e. sent − committed − GAP-covered = 0 (`lost=0`). The script also checks N = B − A + 1 (no `seq` reused) and that the log starts at A, since this run's log starts empty.
  - **Negative control (2026-10-26):** a scratch build of the feed that always continued from the reply + 1 passed every per-round check in `kill9 5`, but failed the final check ("1600 records in 0..1165").
- **(N, T) settings (PF-11):** `build/storage_main -n 1 -t 1 $D/log $S` with `build/storage_feed $S 50 10`. `storage_start` shows `batch_n=1 batch_t_s=1`, and the log holds about 50 `storage_commit records=1` lines: one fsync per record, not one per second.
- **Power pulls (on the Pi, by hand, 20 times):**
  1. Image the SD card first, so a damaged card can be restored.
  2. Start `storage_main /var/lib/plantpi /run/plantpi/storage.sock` and `storage_feed /run/plantpi/storage.sock 100000 50`.
  3. Pull the USB-C cable at a random moment. Note the time since the last `storage_start` or commit, so the results can say how many pulls really landed mid-batch.
  4. Boot, start `storage_main` (expect `unclean_shutdown`, maybe `recovery_event`), stop it, then run `log_verify /var/lib/plantpi`.
  5. Target: `log_verify` passes every time; loss ≤ one unsynced batch (the `seq_resume` gap to the feed's last sent `seq` is ≤ 64 records or 60 s).

## Not done yet (Mechanism D)
- **Disk full and read-only file system:** `ENOSPC`, the 64 KB `statvfs` reserve, and `EROFS` (`storage_disk_full`, `storage_readonly`). Each needs a "disk full" status out of the file seam first.
- **The hub side of hop 2:** reading `seq_resume` and picking the next `seq` by the max rule (Decisions, PF-03), and the 1024-record queue (see *Not done yet* above).
- **The heartbeat to `sup.sock`:** Mechanism E. Proposed to come from the rx thread (*Decisions*, PF-10, pending Lucas).
- **The clock wait, on the Pi:** on an empty log `storage_main` now waits up to 120 s for the clock (PF-20), but WSL's clock is always synced, so the wait has not been seen running. Check it on the Pi with the network unplugged.
- **On-Pi runs:** the fault rounds and power pulls above.

## Log (Mechanism D)
- **2026-10-26:** Mechanism D planned and built in one day on `Menu-Mechanism-D`: Steps 1–13b above, 308 tests across 42 binaries, all green under `make test`, `make asan` and `make memcheck` in WSL and in CI. DESIGN.md brought in line with what was built (pending buffer, retention rule, recovery order, lock before open, `seq_resume` format and its last-accepted `seq`, `storage.sock` as `SOCK_SEQPACKET`, new log events).

  Surprises:
  - `gmtime_r` can't name a segment after 2038 on 32-bit Pi OS, so dates are computed with integer arithmetic.
  - `renameat` is declared in `<stdio.h>`; the build would have failed in WSL without it.
  - GitHub CI (gcc) failed on `-Wformat-truncation` in a test's clean-up path that clang on the Mac accepted; fixed by deleting files with `unlinkat` instead of building paths. Two other spots were hardened the same way (`memcpy` of a measured length in `list`; an unsigned comparison in SAP's helper).
  - SOP-01 first checked durability with `fake_fs_power_cut()` and then closed storage, which a real power cut can't follow; it now checks the fake's synced copy.
  - Step 10's events changed what SAP-08/09 expected (`QUEUE_FULL` on the first refusal, `BACKLOG` while filling); both were updated with approval to expect the exact events.
  - A rollover while degraded would have stranded torn bytes in yesterday's segment, which recovery never revisits; found while writing Step 11 and fixed test-first as Step 11b.
  - macOS has no `SOCK_SEQPACKET` for local sockets, no `SOCK_CLOEXEC` / `MSG_NOSIGNAL`, and its leak checker hangs on tests that `fork()`; the socket tests (LBD, SSV) run only on Linux.

  Next: run `storage_faults.sh` in WSL and the power pulls on the Pi, then the hub's hop-2 sender (or Mechanism E).

### Fault isolation and restart (Mechanism E)

These tests check the *Mechanism E* rows. They run against the processes that exist at each milestone (`light_sensor`, `soil_sensor`, `hub`, `storage`), and `care` and `monitor` are added to the target list when they land. Every run ends with the verifier, so a fault that "recovers" but loses or corrupts data still fails.

| Measurement | Method | Target |
|---|---|---|
| **Containment:** a crash affects only its target | 50 `kill -9`s per process at random times during real-rate logging; check every other PID before and after | Only the targeted PID changes; 0 unrelated exits or restarts |
| **Crash detection and restart time:** `SIGKILL` → `child_exit` → new child sends its first heartbeat | Fault-injector timestamp vs. supervisor log, over the same 50 kills per process | 100% detected; p99 < 2 s from kill to first heartbeat (first restart, before backoff grows) |
| **Hang detection:** `SIGSTOP` → `heartbeat_timeout` → `SIGKILL` → restart | 20 injected hangs per process | 100% detected; detection ≤ 6 s (5 s heartbeat timeout + 1 s heartbeat period); healthy again < 2 s after detection |
| **Peer reconnect:** restarted socket owner → clients send again | Kill the hub 50 times and storage 50 times; measure the time from the new socket appearing to each client's first successful `send()` (`ipc_reconnect`, `storage_reconnected`) | 100% reconnect with no manual action; ≤ 2 s (the client backoff cap) |
| **Readings survive a hub restart** | During the 50 hub kills, compare each sensor's counter against the committed log | 0 lost light or soil readings, because the sensor ring (64 readings ≈ 64 s of light) outlasts a < 2 s restart |
| **Sensor collection continues while a peer is down** | Kill or `SIGSTOP` storage (and later `care` / `monitor`) for 60 s | Hub keeps receiving at 1 Hz light with no `sensor_timeout`; sensors never block on `send()` |
| **No restart storm** | Point one child at a binary that exits at once; run for 10 min | Restart gaps follow 1 → 2 → 4 … capped at 30 s (≤ 25 restarts in 10 min); healthy processes keep their heartbeats and the sampling-jitter target |
| **Cold start after power loss** | The same 20 power pulls as *Data loss*; timestamp supervisor start and each child's first heartbeat | All children heartbeating within 10 s of supervisor start, in dependency order (storage → hub → sensors), on every pull |
| **Protocol robustness** | Unit tests plus a fuzz run of 10,000 random, truncated, wrong-sensor-ID and out-of-range 16 B messages into `hub.sock` | 100% rejected and logged as `ipc_bad_message` or `reading_invalid`; 0 hub crashes; 0 rejected messages stored |
| **Failures are visible** | Every injection above is matched against the event log | 100% of injections produce a process-specific `child_exit`, `heartbeat_timeout`, `ipc_disconnect` or degraded event; 0 silent failures |

### Sensor reliability

This covers the *Failure-mode table → Sensor (I2C)* and *Hub (sensor goes quiet)* rows.

| Measurement | Method | Target |
|---|---|---|
| I2C read failure rate | Count `i2c_read_error` and skipped samples per sensor over the 72 h soak | Report the first-attempt failure rate; < 0.1% of samples skipped after 3 retries |
| Retry, skip and offline logic | Fake I2C bus fails the Nth operation: a single failure, 3 failures in a row, 10 in a row, then recovery | Single failures are recovered by retry with no skipped sample; skip after 3 retries; `sensor_offline` after 10 consecutive failures; `sensor_online` on the first good read |
| Unplug and replug on the real Pi | Pull each sensor's STEMMA cable for 60 s, 10 times per sensor | Hub logs `sensor_timeout` within its timeout + 1 s (3 s light, 180 s soil); other sensor unaffected; `sensor_online` ≤ 6 s after replug (5 s retry period); 0 process crashes |
| Bring-up check | `light_probe` (and a soil probe when the driver lands) on each fresh install | All checklist steps PASS |

These measurements show the raw counts mean something before the analysis engine relies on them. The method and spread are reported along with pass/fail, because the reference instruments are cheap.

| Measurement | Method | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Light accuracy | BH1750 next to a reference lux meter at 5 levels (dark room, indoor lamp, shaded window, bright window, direct sun); 60 readings per level | Within ±20% of the reference at every level (BH1750 datasheet tolerance) |
| Light repeatability | 60 readings at 1 Hz under constant lamp light | Coefficient of variation < 2% |
| Soil calibration points | Raw count in open air, in dry potting mix and in fully watered potting mix; 30 readings each | The three ranges don't overlap; dry < watered; recorded as the calibration constants |
